reviewedRanges.purpose: Native rename attempts, bounded retry policy and pre-cleanup path observations
SDK staging validation, original error preservation and cleanup failure attachment
CLI original stderr line, structured diagnostics and nonzero exit
Complete synthetic staging fixture and four failure diagnostics test declarations

checks.contract: Original rename Error identity and native fields
checks.staticConclusion: Terminal rename failure rethrows the same Error instance. The added publication property does not overwrite message, code, errno or syscall. The original Error is saved before finally cleanup.

Windows EPERM/EACCES still permit six total attempts with five delays of 30, 60, 90, 120 and 150 ms, totaling 450 ms. Other native codes, missing stage or existing output terminate under the prior conditions.

checks.contract: Diagnostics precede cleanup and cannot create a successful result
checks.staticConclusion: Terminal failure records native attempt snapshots and lstat-derived path kinds before pack cleanup. Path-observation failure is represented as unreadable; diagnostic attachment is guarded and the original error is still thrown. No lock-owner attribution is claimed.
When cleanup also throws, pack attaches cleanupFailure and preserves the original Error. It does not retry removal. Cleanup-only failure still throws.

Native diagnostics consist of ordinary serializable fields. The existing SDK error line is emitted before structured diagnostics and exitCode is set to 1; no packed success value is emitted on this path.

Rename mocks trigger only for the exact fixture output. The lstat diagnostic-denial mock remains inactive until the publication rename fails, so source enumeration, safePath and readPackage complete before injection. Filesystem mocks are restored in finally blocks.

limitations: This is a static review only. The four declared tests and CLI child process were not executed by this reviewer.

A real recursive removal can delete some stage members before throwing. The implementation retains the original error and any remaining stage; it does not guarantee a byte-complete immutable failed-stage snapshot. The cleanup-denied test injects failure before deletion.
The source of historical Windows EPERM directory rename failures remains unknown. Diagnostics and first-error preservation do not establish a lock owner or close that root-cause issue.
The pins and reviewed line ranges apply only to the exact file bytes listed above. Later source or test edits require a fresh review or explicit scope update.
